subject: physics
question_text: Explain the following processes: (i) isochoric process (ii) isobaric process.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Very Short Answer Question 14 (printed p.125), printed as one question with two parts: 'Explain the following processes. i) Isochoric process ii) Isobaric process.' Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: an isochoric process has W = 0 and ΔQ = ΔU because the volume is fixed; an isobaric process has W = PΔV and ΔQ = ΔU + PΔV because the pressure is fixed while the volume is free to change.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Isochoric process
lines: In an isochoric process the volume

steps.margin_note: W = 0, ΔQ = ΔU, and the closed rigid vessel example together are the first mark.
steps.why: Volume fixed means the boundary does not move, so W = PΔV is zero automatically — that is what makes ΔQ = ΔU the whole content of the first law here.
common_mistakes: Saying no heat is exchanged in an isochoric process. It is the work that is zero, not the heat.
Giving an example where the vessel is open or flexible. It must be closed and rigid for the volume to stay constant.

steps.label: Isobaric process
lines: In an isobaric process the pressure
the heat supplied is shared between
heating water in an open vessel at
steps.margin_note: W = PΔV, ΔQ = ΔU + PΔV, and the open-vessel example together are the second mark.
steps.why: Pressure fixed lets the volume change freely, so the gas both warms and expands — the heat supplied must now cover both the rise in internal energy and the work of that expansion.
common_mistakes: Writing W = 0 for an isobaric process. Volume changes here, so work is done; it is pressure that is held constant.
Leaving out the PΔV term and writing ΔQ = ΔU alone — that relation is for the isochoric process.
steps.memory_tip: Isobaric: constant pressure, so W = PΔV, not zero.

insider_note: One printed question, two parts: keep W = 0 for isochoric and W = PΔV for isobaric straight, and give a distinct example for each.
